title_guess: Growth, contraction and recession read off a quarterly GDP curve

segments.teaches: GDP is tracked quarter by quarter; the curve rises, peaks and falls over about two years

elements.what: dotted axes, GDP on y, nine quarters on x; black line through yellow-ringed points rising to a peak then falling; red dotted drop lines from each point to the axis
quarter labels tinted by year: first year blue, second year yellow, third year green

segments.notes: One graph is the whole video; every later segment only adds a moving frame or label on top of it.
segments.idea: GDP is tracked quarter by quarter; the curve rises, peaks and falls over about two years
segments.shown_as: dotted axes with GDP up and nine quarters across; a black line through yellow-ringed points rises to a peak and falls, with red dotted drop lines from each point and quarter labels tinted by year

segments.teaches: a rising stretch is growth; the slope tells whether it is faster or slower growth

elements.what: grey rectangular frame tilted to the slope, placed over one rising line piece and then moved to the next piece
green 'growing' label written along the frame
small hand-written note above it: at a faster rate (green), later swapped to at a slower rate (red)

segments.notes: Sliding-window trick: the same frame steps along the curve one quarter at a time and its label changes with the slope.
segments.idea: a rising stretch is growth; its slope shows faster or slower growth
segments.shown_as: a grey frame tilted to the slope sits on one rising piece, then steps to the next; a green 'growing' label runs along it and a handwritten note swaps from 'faster rate' (green) to 'slower rate' (red)

segments.teaches: a quarter where GDP falls is a contraction

elements.what: frame moves onto the first falling piece after the peak
white pointer box above it naming the term contraction in red

segments.notes: Label colour flips from green to red as the slope turns negative.
segments.idea: a quarter where GDP falls is a contraction
segments.shown_as: the frame moves onto the first falling piece after the peak with a red 'decline' label and a pointer box naming the contraction

segments.teaches: contraction for two quarters in a row is a recession

elements.what: red translucent band covering two consecutive falling pieces
bold red 'recession' label along the band
pointer box with the two-quarter definition

segments.notes: The grey frame widens and turns into a red shaded band. Depression, named in the title, does not appear in the sampled frames.
segments.idea: two falling quarters in a row make a recession
segments.shown_as: the frame widens into a red translucent band over two falling pieces in a row, labelled 'recession', with a pointer box giving the two-quarter rule

recurring_cast: graph_axes: one quarterly GDP curve for the whole video
running_examples: nine quarters of GDP rising to a peak, then falling

best_moments.why: a frame steps along the curve and its label changes with the slope
the frame widens into a red band over two falling quarters: recession = two contractions in a row

weak_moments.why: 34 s spent drawing axes and labels before any term is taught
depression, named in the title, is never shown before the end card
